record.question:
A serverless discussion application uses API Gateway, Lambda, and DynamoDB. Clients currently retrieve comments with repeated GET requests. The company wants authorized clients viewing a topic to receive new comments as they are posted, without polling. The team can adopt GraphQL and change the comment-write API, and it wants managed connection handling.

Which solution best meets these requirements?

options.text: Enable API Gateway caching for GET requests and shorten the cache time-to-live so clients receive newer comments on their next request.
Increase Lambda reserved concurrency and have clients poll the existing GET endpoint every second.
Use AWS AppSync GraphQL mutations to create comments and subscriptions to deliver matching updates over WebSocket connections. Authenticate subscribers and authorize access to the requested topics.
Write comments directly to DynamoDB and enable an AppSync subscription, without connecting a comment mutation or event-publishing path to those writes.

explanation.text:
<<3>> is correct. AppSync manages WebSocket connections for GraphQL subscriptions, and configured mutations trigger subscription updates. The write path must execute the relevant mutation, with authorization and filters that ensure a client receives only permitted topic data.

<<1>> changes read caching but still requires the client to request updates. Caching can also return stale comments during the cache lifetime.

<<2>> adds execution capacity but retains polling and its repeated requests.

<<4>> omits the event path. Writing to a DynamoDB table does not by itself trigger a GraphQL subscription merely because AppSync can read that table.

Push delivery and data retrieval solve different needs: use a query for initial state and a subscription for subsequent updates. A custom API Gateway WebSocket solution can also provide push, but the proposed AppSync design supplies managed GraphQL subscription integration.

Official AWS references (checked September 18, 2026): [AppSync GraphQL subscriptions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/appsync/latest/devguide/aws-appsync-real-time-data.html).

diagram_alt: AppSync sends updates through an authorized subscription when the associated mutation executes; initial queries remain separate.

sources.supports: Managed secure WebSocket updates, mutation triggers, and subscription authorization

editorial_notes: Preserved answer 3. Explicitly tied subscription updates to mutations and authorization; removed irrelevant API-key detail and avoided claiming AppSync is the only possible push architecture.
